calls.title: GB x BoyleSports: HP Experiments
calls.summary: The team discussed multiple strategies to improve user engagement and betting conversion rates through website modifications. They decided to test the removal of a redundant bet slip button, verifying its impact on betting activity, while using visual editing for rapid rollout and feature flags for more complex changes. A phased rollout is planned, starting with 10% of traffic, allowing them to monitor key metrics closely. Additionally, they aim to clarify navigation by renaming the 'A to Z list' icon to 'Search' and plan for a full search bar in the future. The team is also launching casino games from navigation to cross-sell to users based on segmentation, ensuring that sports betting engagement metrics remain protected during the process.
calls.keywords: Homepage experiments, bet slip button, visual editor, feature flags, power calculations, personalization targeting
calls.action_items:
**Mark Phillips**
Set up and run the experiment to hide the bet slip button in the global header using the visual editor to validate user behavior and ensure no drop in betting activity (04:48)
Rename the bottom navigation icon from “A to Z list” to “Search” using the visual editor and monitor changes in user interaction to improve click-through rates (10:46)
Implement and test the new casino game launch feature with two separate icons (slots and roulette) initially, planning for future personalized targeting variants via feature flags (17:03)
Define and monitor guardrail metrics such as bets per customer and bounce rates to ensure that the new casino content does not negatively impact sportsbook engagement or user experience (19:12)
Coordinate with analytics and data science teams to perform power calculations to optimize experiment duration and traffic allocation for risk-managed phased rollouts (23:40)

**Joe Taylor**
Assist with implementing visual editor changes for the bet slip button removal and search icon rename to expedite deployment processes (09:56)
Facilitate access to Slack channels for Growth Book support to provide live assistance during experiment setup and troubleshooting (20:50)

**Cris Dizon**
Provide ongoing support via Slack for experiment setup, best practices, monitoring guidance, and share resources on power calculations and rollout strategies (20:36)
